h2: Eddy current testing in Vancouver: Canadian certification after the CGSB change, and how ET jobs are scoped
html:
Eddy current testing in Vancouver: Canadian certification after the CGSB change, and how ET jobs are scoped

For eddy current work in Vancouver, the first question is usually which certification the job requires, because many Canadian owners and codes call for NRCan-certified personnel to CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712). That scheme is confirmed at quotation for every Canadian job. Atlantis provides ET procedures, technique review and reporting under an ASNT NDT Level III, and scopes tube and surface work once material, access and the governing code are known.

What the CGSB wind-down means. The federal government decided in Budget 2025 to wind down the Canadian General Standards Board, effective April 1, 2026. NRCan's National Non-Destructive Testing Certification Body (NDTCB) has stated that its certification programs will continue without interruption, and that CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712, IDT) remains active and valid. The Standards Council of Canada has extended the standard's maintenance deadline, originally October 31, 2027, by two years once ISO publishes a reaffirmation or new edition of ISO 9712, and ISO begins its systematic review in October 2026. NRCan, through CanmetMATERIALS, is setting up a limited-scope standards development organization for the NDT-related CGSB standards; the NDTCB will remain a certification body only.

For a BC owner or contractor, the practical result is simple:

  • NRCan NDT certificates already held stay valid, and renewals continue as before
  • Specifications and procedures that cite CAN/CGSB-48.9712 do not need rewriting now
  • Watch for a new edition after the ISO review, and update references when it is published
  • The NDTCB also runs the written examination for CNSC exposure device operator certification, which matters if the same crew will do radiography

How Vancouver ET jobs are scoped. Where a plant cools with seawater or brackish water, exchanger and condenser tubes are often copper-nickel, titanium or stainless, which suit conventional bobbin ECT; carbon steel tubes in process service need remote field testing, near-field testing or IRIS instead. Surface ET finds fatigue cracks at weld toes and around fasteners through thin paint, which helps on marine structure and on equipment exposed to salt air, where stripping coating invites new corrosion. For each job, define the tube material and size or the component and coating, the calibration standard with its artificial flaws, the cleaning required before probes will pass, and who analyzes the data and signs the result.

Pressure equipment in BC. Boilers, pressure vessels and pressure piping are registered and inspected under provincial safety legislation that references CSA B51. Tube findings and plugging records become part of that equipment's file, so reports should identify each tube by row and column and carry the technician's certification and the reference standard used.

Method background is on the eddy current testing page, and steel exchanger tubes that need a measured remaining wall are covered by IRIS tube inspection. Companies writing or updating an ET procedure or written practice for Canadian work can use outsourced ASNT NDT Level III consulting. Technicians can study through ET training and the Practical NDT eddy current simulator; see NDT training in Canada for how that fits the Canadian scheme. To scope a Vancouver job, send tube or component details and dates through the Vancouver ET request.
